tasks.title: The first view
tasks.statement: Create a view vip_customers: id, name, city of the VIP customers only (vip = 1). The result is checked by a query to the view.
tasks.hint: A view is a saved query; you can refer to it like a table.

tasks.title: Expensive products
tasks.statement: Create a view expensive_products(id, title, price) for products costing more than 5000.

tasks.title: Hide extra columns
tasks.statement: Create a view customers_public (id, name, city) — without email and registration date.
tasks.hint: This is how you close off sensitive columns.

tasks.title: Selecting from a view
tasks.statement: The database already has a view paid_orders (paid orders). Output id and total of the orders with a sum greater than 5000 from it; order by id.
tasks.hint: You can work with a view like with an ordinary table: WHERE, ORDER BY, JOIN.

tasks.title: A view with JOIN
tasks.statement: Create a view order_details(order_id, customer, created, total): the order number, the customer's name, the date and the amount (JOIN orders and customers).

tasks.title: Detailed line items
tasks.statement: Create a view item_lines(order_id, title, qty, line_total): order items with the product title and the amount qty * price.

tasks.title: A view with an aggregate
tasks.statement: Create a view customer_stats(customer_id, orders_n, revenue): the number of orders and the sum per customer (GROUP BY customer_id).

tasks.title: Using a view
tasks.statement: There is a view customer_stats(customer_id, orders_n, revenue). Output name and revenue of customers with revenue > 10000 (JOIN the view with customers); order by name.

tasks.title: Column names in parentheses
tasks.statement: Column names can be given as a list: CREATE VIEW v (a, b) AS …. Create a view prices (title_ru, price_rub) from products (title, price).

tasks.title: Calculated columns
tasks.statement: Create a view product_value(id, title, stock_value), where stock_value = price * stock.

tasks.title: CASE in a view
tasks.statement: Create a view order_labels(id, total, size): size = `'large'` when total ≥ 40000, `'medium'` when ≥ 5000, otherwise `'small'`.

tasks.title: A view reflects the data
tasks.statement: Create a view new_orders (id, total) for the status 'new', then ship order 6 (UPDATE status = 'shipped'). A view is always recomputed: it must still contain 11 and 17, 20.

tasks.title: A view over a view
tasks.statement: There is a view paid_orders. On top of it create big_paid(id, total) — paid orders over 5000.

tasks.title: IF NOT EXISTS
tasks.statement: Create the view v_vip twice in a row with IF NOT EXISTS — without an error: id, name of the VIP customers.

tasks.title: Dropping a view
tasks.statement: The database has a view old_report. Drop it (DROP VIEW). The list of views is checked.

tasks.title: DROP VIEW IF EXISTS
tasks.statement: Safely drop the view tmp_v (DROP VIEW IF EXISTS), and then create it again: the ids of products with stock 0.

tasks.title: Changing a view
tasks.statement: A view can't be changed with ALTER — it is re-created. Drop v_cheap and create it again with the threshold 1000 instead of 500.

tasks.title: Where the definition is
tasks.statement: A view's definition is stored in sqlite_master. Output the name and type of the view order_report: SELECT name, type FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'order_report'.

tasks.title: List of views
tasks.statement: Output the names of all views in the database in alphabetical order (type = 'view').

tasks.title: A temporary view
tasks.statement: Create a temporary view (CREATE TEMP VIEW) top3_expensive: title, price of the three most expensive products.

tasks.title: A view and a window function
tasks.statement: Create a view ranked_products(category, title, price, rk): the product's place in its category by descending price (RANK).

tasks.title: A view as row protection
tasks.statement: The manager of the city `'Moscow'` should see only the customers from that city. Create a view moscow_customers (id, name, email) and check it with a select.

tasks.title: A view and masking
tasks.statement: Create a view masked_customers (id, name, email_masked): email_masked is the first letter + '***' + the part starting from '@'; NULL for customers without an email.

tasks.title: Changing through a trigger
tasks.statement: A view doesn't update by itself. Create a view v_stock (id, title, stock) and an INSTEAD OF UPDATE trigger that carries the change of stock over to the products table, then run UPDATE v_stock SET stock = 99 WHERE id = 6.
tasks.hint: An INSTEAD OF trigger runs instead of the operation on the view.

tasks.title: A report view
tasks.statement: Create a view revenue_by_category(category, revenue): revenue per category (order_items JOIN products, SUM(qty * price)).

tasks.title: Using the report
tasks.statement: There is a view revenue_by_category. Output the categories with revenue above the average across categories; order by category.

tasks.title: HR: public directory
tasks.statement: HR database. Create a view staff_directory(id, name, dept, email): the employee and the department name (LEFT JOIN, NULL for those without a department), without salary and phone.

tasks.title: HR: department statistics
tasks.statement: HR database. Create a view dept_stats(dept, staff, payroll): the number of employees and the payroll by department (only departments that have employees).

tasks.title: HR: a view for a manager
tasks.statement: HR database. Create a view my_team (id, name, salary) — the subordinates of Nina Belova (boss_id = 5) — and select from it the employees with a salary above 100000; order by id.

tasks.title: School: gradebook
tasks.statement: School database. Create a view gradebook(student, course, score, year): the student's and the course's names and the grade (JOIN of three tables).

tasks.title: School: top students
tasks.statement: School database. Create a view honors(student, avg_score): students whose average score for 2024 is at least 4.5 (ROUND to 2 digits).

tasks.title: Movies: a selection
tasks.statement: Movies database. Create a view top_movies(title, year, rating, director): movies with a rating ≥ 8 and the director's name (JOIN).

tasks.title: Movies: using the selection
tasks.statement: Movies database. There is a view top_movies(title, year, rating, director). Output the directors and the number of their movies from the view as n; order by n descending, then director.
